no-magic-numbers.note: ALLOWED_NODES coverage (ExportAssignment, PropertyAssignment/Shorthand, VariableDeclaration(List), EnumMember, PropertyDeclaration, Parameter default) and the -1/0/1 default-allowed check on numeric text (incl. negative-unary anchoring) match TSLint exactly; verified export=, class field, enum member, parameter default and negative-literal cases all agree. One obscure divergence: TSLint's own isAllowedNumber does `parseFloat(node.text)`, so a hex literal like `0x10` parses to 0 and is spuriously allowed by TSLint's own bug; the port correctly flags it, which is arguably more correct, not less.

ban-ts-ignore.note: Regex on every comment node matches TSLint's forEachComment scan.

ban-types.note: Structure genuine (excludes self-declarations, heritage targets, qualified names) but TSLint's default bans nothing; the doc bakes the fixture's String/Object/Fo* list.

no-for-in.note: kind+regex bans all for-in, as TSLint does.

no-import-side-effect.note: Default doc bans all side-effect imports (TSLint's default); ignore-module override models the option.

no-inferrable-types.note: Default and option variants match shouldCheck/typeIsInferrable on extra cases too: readonly/override matched as modifier tokens, numeric initializers under any unary +/- chain.

no-internal-module.note: Kind split encodes TSLint's Namespace/GlobalAugmentation checks.

no-namespace.note: Top-level-only scope reproduces TSLint's walk; allow-declarations excludes .d.ts.

no-reference.note: Scans raw content for `/// <reference path=` instead of the compiler's referencedFiles; confirmed a string literal containing that text is not flagged (this port scope is per-file regex over content, so a string literal WOULD in fact be false-flagged in general use -- see sidecar; keep as regex-capture-anchor primary already recorded).

no-reference-import.note: The directive is a `///` comment before the first statement (comments and a shebang may precede it, as the compiler reads pragmas from the leading comments), its `types` value is read out of the comment by a `transform` and compared with every static import's specifier (import declarations and import-equals, at the top level and in ambient modules: findImports(AllStaticImports)). Verified re-exports, dynamic imports, `path` references, unclosed directives and directives after the first statement are not flagged. Residual: a specifier written with escapes (`"b\u0061z"`) compares by its source fragments, not its value.

no-var-requires.note: Exemption list includes pair and parenthesized_expression; confirmed `var cfg = { b: require("b") }; var c = (require("c"));` -> no findings although TSLint would flag both.

only-arrow-functions.note: functionIsExempt as TSLint: generators (distinct kinds), a leading `this` parameter, or `this` in the body outside nested scopes with their own `this` (hasOwnThisReference: classes, function declarations/expressions, object-literal methods), found by a has walk with that stopBy rule; overload and ambient signatures are flagged as FunctionDeclarations. Verified `function outer(){ function inner(){ this.y } }` flags outer, and an object-literal method's `this` does not exempt its enclosing function.

promise-function-async.note: Syntactic proxy for the inferred return type (sidecar already documents this); misses `function foo(){ return fetch(url).then(r => r.json()); }`.

ban-comma-operator.note: Isolates the for-incrementor comma expression as TSLint's parent.incrementor check does.

ban.note: Structure genuine (name-blind call/property-chain text match, wildcard handled) but TSLint's default list is empty; the doc bakes the fixture's list.

curly.note: ignore-same-line tests whether the whole if_statement text is single-line; confirmed a wrapped condition with a one-line body is wrongly flagged.

forin.note: has continue_statement anywhere in the if subtree; confirmed nested continue inside a deeper if is still treated as filtered (should only count a direct/blocked continue in the then-branch) -- port is looser than TSLint but same direction of error, no FN found in the direct case; treat as fixture-fit since TSLint's own filter is stricter (an else-branch continue, sibling structure) and the port's has() search is unscoped.

function-constructor.note: Name-blind Function call/new match, as TSLint.

label-position.note: for-of shares for_in_statement kind, so the allowed-kind list covers it.

no-arg.note: Literal arguments.callee pattern, as TSLint's text check.

no-bitwise.note: Expression-kind operators only; type-position &/|are distinct kinds.

no-conditional-assignment.note: stopBy:end gate reproduces TSLint's checking/noCheck propagation.

no-console.note: Default bans all console.* (TSLint default); list override for the option.

no-construct.note: new String/Number/Boolean by identifier text, as TSLint.

adjacent-overload-signatures.note: Key (normalised name, static-ness, call/construct by kind) bound once and compared with earlier siblings; the previous-member walk is a recursive util skipping any run of ;/,/comments (and accessors under ignore-accessors). Numeric names compare by source text.

unified-signatures.note: Any list length: $$$PRE/$$$POST captures align the other overload's parameter list. Parameters around the differing one compare by full text (TSLint: sigils + type), so overloads that differ also in a parameter name are missed; all unifiable pairs reported (TSLint: first pair per 3+ group).

prefer-for-of.note: Index uses resolved syntactically: nearer let/const/var/parameter declarations inside the loop shadow; catch parameters, destructured declarations and var hoisting into nested functions are not modelled.

no-unsafe-finally.note: Nearest-boundary walk expressed as not-inside a local boundary that is itself inside the finally block; labeled jumps compare the bound label.

prefer-readonly.note: Receiver of a write decided syntactically (this, `const x = this` aliases, the class name) where TSLint uses its type; writes through other references to the class are missed.

prefer-function-over-method.note: Own-this boundaries scoped to the bound method text; recursion compares the member name with the bound method name (string-literal method names are compared with quotes).

completed-docs.note: Tag existence/content requirements are regexes over the whole comment text; a tag mentioned inside another tag's description satisfies them.

no-parameter-reassignment.note: Target name joined to an enclosing function's parameter names; a nearer declaration shadowing the parameter is not modelled.

no-switch-case-fall-through.note: endsControlFlow (no checker) as recursive utils: loops, try/finally, collected breaks, constant conditions; a labeled statement ends unless a break/continue carrying its own label (shared binding inside a `not`) is inside it, as matchLabel. Verified `L: { break L; }` falls through, `N: for(;;) { break O; }` does not. Residual: a labeled jump counts wherever it is in the labeled statement, reachable or not.

no-default-export.note: Anchors the `default` keyword of a top-level export statement; .d.ts excluded by scope.

no-duplicate-imports.note: Module text bound once and compared with earlier imports in the same list; external-module files share the list with string-named ambient modules, as walkWorker reuses `seen`.

no-mergeable-namespace.note: Head identifier of each namespace name bound and compared with earlier sibling module declarations, as checkStatements keeps `seen` per statement list.

no-duplicate-switch-case.note: Case value bound once and compared by text with the value of every earlier sibling case, as TSLint compares getText().

no-duplicate-super.note: Sibling-scoped reachability: a compound statement containing return/throw/break anywhere (including a nested function's return) ends the sequence, where TSLint combines branches with worse(); labeled breaks are treated as plain breaks.

no-dynamic-delete.note: Narrow ASCII regex stands in for isValidPropertyAccess; confirmed `delete obj["café"]` is not flagged though TSLint would flag it.

no-empty.note: Brace-only regex plus constructor/catch/function exclusions mirror isExcluded.

no-misused-new.note: Return type name (plain or generic, identifier only) bound once and compared with the declaring interface or class name, as returnTypeMatchesParent does.

no-null-keyword.note: null outside literal_type and strict comparisons, as TSLint.

no-null-undefined-union.note: Needs the type checker for aliased/inferred-return unions; the port sees explicit A|null|undefined syntax, flattened through nesting and parentheses to any depth by recursive utils. `function get(c){ if(c) return null; return undefined; }` (inferred null|undefined return) is a real FN.

no-object-literal-type-assertion.note: Exemption regex requires only whitespace between `as` and the keyword; `{} as /* keep */ any` breaks the match and is wrongly flagged (confirmed).

no-return-await.note: Tail-position walk and try/catch exemption are recursive utils that stop at the enclosing function, as TSLint's; awaits over as/satisfies are exempt because tree-sitter binds the assertion inside the await.

no-submodule-imports.note: Empty default whitelist matches TSLint's default; regex plus static/dynamic import and require() coverage mirrors findImports/isSubmodulePath.

no-tautology-expression.note: $A op $A plus depth-1 operand-kind restriction mirrors TSLint's identifier/property-access/literal checks.

no-this-assignment.note: variable_declarator + depth-1 has kind:this reproduces TSLint's "initializer is a bare this" check exactly.

no-unused-expression.note: TSLint's checking walk (parens, void, ternary branches, comma operands, fast-null && / ||) is recursive utils to any depth; directive prologues are every leading string statement, as TSLint scans them.

no-var-keyword.note: declare var / declare global { var } exclusions match TSLint's isGlobalVarDeclaration exactly.

prefer-conditional-expression.note: Recursive utils follow the else-if chain to any length sharing $X; chain links skipped as TSLint's walk does.

prefer-object-spread.note: The "used-result" purity check is a regex limited to bare identifier/dotted-property chains; `Object.assign(cache[key], extra)` is missed.

radix.note: Mirrors TSLint's 6 checked call forms and the single-argument restriction.

static-this.note: TSLint resets its context at every class member: the inside walk stops at the nearest class member (stopBy rule) and tests it for `static`. Verified a static method of a class nested in an instance method is flagged, and an instance field of a class nested in a static method is not.

switch-default.note: Two-level direct-child chain correctly scopes to the switch's own clauses.

triple-equals.note: Default doc flags every bare ==/!= unconditionally (TSLint's true default); overrides exempt only literal null/undefined operands.

typeof-compare.note: Operator set and faulty-result/legal-result lists match TSLint's isFaultyTypeofResult/LEGAL_TYPEOF_RESULTS exactly.

unnecessary-constructor.note: Default (empty-body) doc is genuine; check-super-calls override enumerates forwarding-super-call parameter counts by regex only up to 6 params.

use-isnan.note: All 8 relational/equality operators and the plain-identifier NaN check match TSLint's isExpressionNaN exactly.

invalid-void.note: Structural placement checks plus the generics gate match TSLint's failedKinds set and allow-generics option.

member-ordering.note: Port genuine under an order option, but TSLint's bare `true` reports nothing (parseOptions throws "Got empty options"); the default doc bakes the fields-first preset. Rank failures against any earlier higher-ranked sibling (TSLint's last non-failing member holds the highest rank); alphabetize compares with any earlier same-rank member whose lower-cased name sorts after (the last non-failing member holds the greatest name of its rank), via a follows whose rule compares, computed names first, getter after same-named setter. Verified `b() a() c() B()` flags a and B.

cyclomatic-complexity.note: Every tsutils function scope boundary (functions, methods, accessors, classes, namespaces, enums, interfaces, signatures, function types) counts TSLint's decision nodes in its own subtree with a count whose has walk stops at nested boundaries. Verified a class whose property initializer has 3 ternaries is reported at threshold 3, and an arrow function's decisions do not count for its enclosing function.

no-invalid-this.note: TSLint's ParentType walk: the nearest class or function-like (arrows transparent) via an inside walk with that stopBy rule; allowed in a class method (a function-like whose own nearest scope is a class) or a `this`-parameter function; check-function-in-method in the override. Effective PASS on the repaired fixture.

comment-format.note: Structure genuine (check-space and check-lowercase with TSLint's exemptions, anchored after the slashes), but bare `true` checks nothing in TSLint; the default doc bakes the common check-space + check-lowercase config. Option variants are overrides.

file-header.note: Port genuine for a given header regex, but that regex is TSLint's mandatory `match` option; the default doc bakes the fixtures' `Good header \d`, so it flags every real file. The first comment after an optional shebang must match the header regex, which is TSLint's required `match` option (each doc carries the fixture's); an empty file and a shebang file report where TSLint does (zero-width, after the shebang line). allow-single-line-comments and the trailing-newline option are overrides.

no-redundant-jsdoc.note: Content regexes per tag family stand in for a JSDoc parse and are not confined to `/** */` comments: `// @param {string} x` or a string containing `@type {x}` is flagged though TSLint only reads JSDoc.

type-literal-delimiter.note: Type literals only (not interfaces): comma separators and a trailing ';' on single-line literals are flagged on the token, a missing delimiter on the member's last character; matches TSLint's default and singleLine options.

number-literal-format.note: Number node + regex per TSLint check (leading 0, lowercase hex digits, leading/trailing decimal point, trailing zeros, exponent leading zeros), with mid-token anchors through named groups.

max-classes-per-file.note: Port genuine per threshold, but the threshold is TSLint's required argument (bare `true` compares against undefined and never fires); the default doc bakes the fixture's 1. Exact document-order count via recursive utils: after-K holds when a class with K-1 classes before it (an ancestor, or at/inside an earlier sibling of the node or any ancestor) precedes the node, to any depth; each threshold is its own doc.

no-default-import.note: TSLint's walk skips .d.ts and non-module files before scanning; the port has no such file-level exclusion.

no-require-imports.note: Bare require($$$A) plus import x = require(...) matches tsutils' findImports(AllRequireLike).

array-type.note: Port genuine per option, but TSLint requires one of array/generic/array-simple (bare `true` flags both T[] and Array<T>); the default doc bakes the fixture's "array". array-simple's isSimpleType (parens, nested Array<T>) is a recursive util, unbounded; verified 5-deep nesting matches TSLint.

arrow-return-shorthand.note: Only-statement test (comments skipped) replaces the kind exclusion list; an unreachable second return is no longer flagged.

binary-expression-operand-order.note: The numeric-literal regex also matches BigInt literals; `1n + a` is a false positive (confirmed).

callable-types.note: Single-member-count structural check plus the extends Function heritage regex reproduces TSLint's checks.

class-name.note: type_identifier scoped via immediate-parent inside to the declaration's own name field.

comment-type.note: Port faithful: bare `true` allows no comment kind, so the default doc flags every comment. An absurd ban; the rule needs an allowed-kinds list. Four mutually-exclusive regexes on raw comment text mirror TSLint's own text-prefix branching.

increment-decrement.note: Default bans all update_expression; allow-post override's prefix-text regex leaves postfix unflagged.

interface-name.note: Regexes behaviorally equivalent to TSLint's hasPrefixI plus its acronym-ambiguity filter.

interface-over-type-literal.note: Flags alias names only when the value is an object_type lacking index_signature/mapped_type_clause.

no-angle-bracket-type-assertion.note: not-inside dedups nested assertion chains, reproducing TSLint's outermost-only collapse at any depth.

no-parameter-properties.note: has(stopBy:neighbor) on accessibility/override/readonly modifiers as direct children of required/optional_parameter matches isParameterProperty.

no-unnecessary-callback-wrapper.note: Self-call exclusion only covers 1-/2-param arity; confirmed `(a, b, c) => c(a, b, c)` is flagged though TSLint's own `expression.text === name.text` bail exempts it, and confirmed `x => (f)(x)` is flagged though TSLint's isIdentifier(callee) check means TSLint itself never even considers it.

no-unnecessary-initializer.note: direct-child undefined check plus arm split (variable_declarator/param/assignment_pattern) mirrors TSLint's real coverage.

object-literal-key-quotes.note: as-needed/consistent-as-needed "valid property name" check is ASCII-only; tsutils' isValidPropertyName is Unicode- and numeric-literal-aware, so e.g. `{"1e4": 1}` is a real miss the fixtures don't exercise.

object-literal-shorthand.note: pair_pattern/shorthand_property_identifier_pattern kinds are shared with destructuring; confirmed `const { a: a } = x;` is flagged as longhand-property though TSLint's PropertyAssignment-based walk never touches destructuring.

one-variable-per-declaration.note: declarator-follows-comma has-check plus export_statement/for_statement split mirrors TSLint's VariableStatement/for-initializer walk.

prefer-method-signature.note: inside(property_signature)+has(type_annotation)+has(function_type) reproduces isPropertySignature+isFunctionTypeNode incl. TSLint's own blind spots.

prefer-template.note: containsAnyStringLiterals/containsOnlyStringLiterals are recursive utils; the outermost offending concatenation is reported over every ancestor.

prefer-while.note: Text regex on the for_statement header stands in for an AST field check; confirmed a comment inside the header (`for (/* i */; i<10;) {}`) breaks the match and the violation is missed.

switch-final-break.note: "always" override checks only literal break/return/throw/continue as the clause's last statement, no recursive endsControlFlow; confirmed `case 0: if(a){throw x}else{throw y}` is flagged though TSLint's endsControlFlow means it should not be.

import-spacing.note: Spacing checks run as unscoped file.content regex with no import_statement guard; confirmed a re-export `export { X } from"./y";` is flagged though TSLint's ImportDeclaration-only walker never inspects export-from statements.

linebreak-style.note: Default/override regexes are exact per-line equivalents of TSLint's CR/LF walk.

new-parens.note: new_expression lacking an arguments child mirrors ts.NewExpression.arguments === undefined exactly.

no-irregular-whitespace.note: Char class reproduces TSLint's IRREGULAR_WHITESPACE_REGEX set, whole-file scope matching TSLint.

arrow-parens.note: ban-single-arg-parens override's textual regex over formal_parameters breaks on a comment inside the parens (`(bar/*x*/) => bar`), missing a violation TSLint's structural isSimpleParameter check would flag. (Effective verdict is PASS (repaired fixture) for the fixture-artifact blocker; this fixture-fit gap is separate and real.)

import-blacklist.note: The implicit-named fallback (whole-module warn on a partially-banned import) is only wired for lodash, not the fixture's own `dummy` module; `import * as x from "dummy";` would be unflagged though TSLint's generic fallback flags any partially-banned module. (Effective verdict PASS (repaired fixture) for the fixture-artifact blocker; primary primitive stays fixture-artifact since option-baking is the more decisive limitation here.) The default doc also bakes the fixture's banned list (lodash, dummy, pull/pullAll), where TSLint's bare `true` bans nothing (found by the harness's `literals` scan).

member-access.note: stopBy:neighbor scoping mirrors TSLint's shouldCheck/check() exactly incl. accessor/constructor/parameter-property variants; both repairs are invalid-syntax (TS1245/TS1029) fixes, not semantic gaps.

newline-per-chained-call.note: hasChildCall's real recursion is unbounded descent through member/subscript chains; a 6-hop chain is a false negative.

no-any.note: TSLint's check is purely syntactic (AnyKeyword); the predefined_type/any match plus rest-arg exclusion is exactly equivalent.

no-async-without-await.note: functionBlockHasAwait/Return is a recursive `has-await-or-return` util that stops at arrow/function-declaration barriers, unbounded; verified an await 20 blocks deep counts.

no-empty-interface.note: extends_type_clause text regex on [,<] is a safe proxy given the grammar; correctly distinguishes single-no-args vs multi/typed extends.

no-string-literal.note: Identifier regex is ASCII-letters/underscore/$ plus \u00XX escapes only; TSLint's isValidPropertyAccess is fully Unicode-aware, so `obj["café"]` is a real miss.

no-string-throw.note: isString recursion through +/paren chains is a recursive `is-string` util, unbounded; verified 8-term concatenation and 7 nested parens are flagged.

no-unnecessary-class.note: Static members decided by the member's own `static` token and constructors by their `constructor` name node (no text regex; decorators with arguments no longer hide static); anchored at the `class` keyword; abstract classes included.

prefer-switch.note: Recursive utils: any-length if/else-if chains and || trees, recursive isSimple, min-cases counted through the chain.

quotemark.note: default/single/double/backtick/avoid-escape/avoid-template/jsx-* overrides each reproduce TSLint's exact escape and backtick-invalid-context logic; the fixture blocker is genuinely invalid-TS syntax errors (repaired-fixture PASS).

typedef.note: TSLint's typedef checks nothing without options, so the default doc is a placeholder check that cannot match; overrides carry the port. Bare-parameter arrow-call-signature starts at the last char of the preceding token (TSLint's parameters.pos - 1), via a named regex group anchor; verified `return n => n`, `async n => n`, template `${n => n}`. End stays one char short of TSLint's (param end + 1).

unnecessary-else.note: Recursive chain util walks the whole direct else-if chain, as recentStackParentMissingJumpStatement.

variable-name.note: Declare skip matches TSLint: only a variable statement directly under `declare` (and its subtree); verified `declare module "m" { export const Bad_Name }` and `declare function f(Bad_Arg)` are flagged, `declare const Bad_Name` is not.
